what: diagnose/repro-mmap-prot.hip.cpp, 32 MiB per copy, gfx1100, VFIO guest. Host-to-device copy time by source mapping, across three kernel states. The bug is the rw-p resident row.
why: The first two states were measured 2026-07-28 and are what the repository published. The third was measured 2026-08-23 on the kernel Canonical actually ships, which until then the repository had only inferred from a changelog entry.

states.note: 16 019.7 = sixteen 1000 ms HMM_RANGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT windows plus 19.7 ms of real work

states.amdgpu: rebuilt from Ubuntu's -28 source with 342981fff328 applied, nothing else changed
states.note: this is what proved the cause; it is not a kernel anyone ships

states.amdgpu: stock, as shipped by Canonical in noble-updates and noble-security
states.note: same machine and same reproducer binary as the 2026-07-28 baseline, re-run the same day before upgrading: 16019.3 ms. The upgrade is the only variable.

reading: Canonical's -30 fixes it. 16019.3 -> 15.3 ms, a factor of 1047, and the two control rows stay in their own range: r--p resident 3.0 to 3.2 ms, rw-p not resident 14.5 to 13.1. The second is a 1.4 ms move, about 10%, in the opposite direction to the bug and small against the 16 s it is a control for, which is what a single-loop fix should look like. The residual writable-mapping penalty survives at 15.3/3.2 = 4.8x, inside the 4-8x band reported earlier, but its absolute size is now about 12 ms per 32 MiB rather than sixteen seconds.
not_established: Nothing outstanding here. The end-to-end loader benchmark was re-run on -30 the same day; see loader-flag-kernel-30.json. The arithmetic guess recorded here first, that 12 ms per 32 MiB would scale to single-digit seconds on a 21.67 GiB checkpoint, was right about the order and wrong about the shape: what the writable mapping costs depends on how large the checkpoint is against host RAM, because breaking copy-on-write converts it into anonymous memory.
